title: fix(runtime): a refused flow resume answers its engine's code — INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT, INVALID_SIGNAL, RUN_NOT_FOUND
body:
Fixes #21724

Clause-②: yes (widening)

A refused flow resume now answers its engine's own code, on the REST resume door and on the MCP `resume_run` tool. Before, it answered a code derived from the HTTP status. No status moves, nothing that was accepted is refused, and a refused resume still leaves the run paused.

## What was wrong, and where the code was lost (A2)

Both doors read one classifier, `classifyResumeResult` in `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`:
- `POST /api/v1/automation/:name/runs/:runId/resume`;
- the MCP `resume_run` tool (`./mcp.ts`).

Both hand its answer to the same `deps.error` builder. The engine's answer was right: it returned `INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT`, `INVALID_SIGNAL` and `RUN_NOT_FOUND`. The builder also behaved as documented: it promotes `details.code`, and it derives a code from the status only when a call site supplies none.

The code was lost at the rows. Each of the six coded rows returned `{ message, status }` with no `details.code`, so the builder fell back to `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap`.

The fix is at that one seat, with no per-door copy:
- a row now returns `details: { code }`, which the builder promotes into `error.code`;
- `ResumeRefusal.details` is now required, so an exit that forgets the code is a compile error instead of a status-derived code.

| Refusal | Status | `error.code` before | `error.code` now |
|---|---|---|---|
| screen input breaks the screen's declared fields | 400 | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | `INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT` |
| signal writes an engine-reserved `$` name | 400 | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | `INVALID_SIGNAL` |
| unknown run / flow gone / paused node edited away | 404 | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | `RUN_NOT_FOUND` |
| suspended-run store unreadable | 503 | `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | `STORE_UNAVAILABLE` |
| another resume holds the run | 409 | `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` | `RESUME_IN_PROGRESS` |
| service-owned suspension | 403 | `PERMISSION_DENIED` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` (unchanged) |

The card names the first three rows. The 503 and 409 rows move by the same one-line fix. The same 17.1.0 changelog sentence and the client JSDoc already promise both codes, and triage's direction ("each refusal row carries its engine code") covers them.

## The flow-gone case (A3): measured in the engine, no engine edit

`packages/services/service-automation` was not edited. `resumeInternal` already returns `code: 'RUN_NOT_FOUND'` in three cases:
- a flow that is no longer registered (`engine.ts:7436`, message "Flow '…' not found for run '…'");
- a suspended node that was edited away (`:7440`);
- an unknown run (`:7411`).

The existing `RUN_NOT_FOUND` row maps all three.

## The ledger (A4)

- **The row.** `INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT` is registered under `@objectstack/service-automation`, beside `INVALID_SIGNAL` (`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, one row).
  - No synonym waiver is needed: no standard member carries the token `SCREEN`.
  - Provenance holds: the stamp site is `service-automation`'s `engine.ts`, which is the row's own owner key.
- **`dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts` needed no new entry; it needed one removed.**
  - Its existing `INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT` row (verdict `foreign-vocabulary`) said the string never lands in `error.code`, and that is now false.
  - Registration made the row stale: `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` printed "[stale-row] … delete the row". The row is deleted.
  - One sibling row's `why` cited that row by name, so it now stands alone.
- **Generated docs.** `gen:docs` regenerated two reference pages: `content/docs/references/api/contract.mdx` and `error-code-ledger.mdx`. Each gains one bullet, and the enum count goes from "+320 more" to "+321 more".

## Measured at the public door (A1, and the door pin after the fix)

Setup:
- the stock showcase, booted twice with `pnpm dev -- --fresh` (the BASE build first, then the fixed build);
- signed in as the seeded admin;
- the card's own steps, scripted;
- the scratch screen flow is created through `POST /api/v1/automation`, triggered, then `DELETE`d.

| Step | BASE `316be321ef` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| resume with `{"inputs":{}}` | 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 `INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT` |
| resume with `output: {"$User":{}}` | 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 `INVALID_SIGNAL` |
| resume `run_nope` | 404 `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 `RUN_NOT_FOUND` |
| resume a run whose flow was deleted | 404 `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 `RUN_NOT_FOUND` |
| `sys_automation_run` status after each refusal | `paused` | `paused` |
| valid resume afterwards | 200, `success: true` | 200, `success: true` |

## Pins

- **`packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-resume-refusal-codes.test.ts` (new).** It is driven from `RESUME_REFUSAL_ROWS` itself (now exported from the domain module; the package index does not re-export it).
  - A floor pins the six rows.
  - Per row, three cases:
    - its key parses as an `ErrorCode`, so a row added without a registered code reds by name;
    - the REST door serves that code, and the body parses under `ApiErrorSchema`;
    - separately, the row keeps its status and message, and `details` stays empty.
- **`packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.test.ts`.**
  - The `.not.toBe('FLOW_FAILED')` assertion is replaced by `toBe('INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT')`.
  - The stale-suspension and `INVALID_SIGNAL` cases now name their codes.
- **`packages/runtime/src/mcp-resume-run.test.ts`.**
  - The door-against-door table names the code for every row. Equality alone held while both doors served the derived code.
  - The CONTROL case named `VALIDATION_ERROR`, which pinned the defect itself. It now names `INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT`.
- **`packages/client/src/automation-resume-refusal-codes.test.ts` (new).**
  - It drives the real `AutomationEngine` with built-in nodes, the real `HttpDispatcher`, and the real `ObjectStackClient`; only the socket is stubbed.
  - Runtime and spec resolve through their BUILT `dist`, so this is the door pin on built packages.
  - Each of the four refusals is pinned twice:
    - the code, on `err.code`, on the wire, and parsed under `ApiErrorSchema`;
    - the status, with the run still `paused`, and a corrected resume completing it where the flow still exists.
- **`packages/client/src/client.test.ts`.** The mocked stale-suspension body said `NOT_FOUND`, a code no door answers. It now uses `RUN_NOT_FOUND` and asserts `err.code`.

## Reverse verification (A5)

Every leg ran through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, against committed head `5f628a7600`, with the direction predicted before running.

**Leg A: the code carry, measured from source.**
- Anchor: `details: { code } };` (1 hit). It was replaced by `details: { code: undefined as unknown as string } };`. Blob `da20e5fca295` → `1d3f06fce818`.
- Run over the runtime pin file, `http-dispatcher.test.ts`, `mcp-resume-run.test.ts` and `automation-resume-stranded-details.test.ts`: **14 failed / 287 passed**.
  - The 14 red, exactly as predicted: 5 row code pins, 3 `http-dispatcher` code assertions, and in MCP 5 coded rows plus CONTROL.
  - Green, as predicted: the 6 status pins, the 6 vocabulary pins, the floor, the stranded-details coded-refusal cases (status plus empty details), and the `FLOW_FAILED` rows.
  - The `PERMISSION_DENIED` row stays green by construction: 403 derives that same code, so no ablation can tell it apart.
- Restore proven: blob == HEAD `da20e5fca295`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

**Leg B: the same mutation, rebuilt into runtime `dist`, measured by the client pin.**
- The mutation was held with a bash trap restore, then `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime build`.
- `dist` emitted `details: { code: void 0 }`. `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs @objectstack/runtime 'status: row.status, details: { code } }' --absent --source-marker='details: { code } };'` exited 0.
- Client: **4 failed / 4 passed**. The 4 code pins failed with "expected 'VALIDATION_ERROR' to be 'INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT'". All 4 status and suspension pins stayed green.
- Restore → rebuild. Preflight `--absent` on `details: { code: void 0 }` exited 0, and present-mode on the fix's carry exited 0 (2 built files). The tree was clean.
- Client after restore: 8/8.

**Leg C: the ledger row deleted.**
- The anchor is the row line (1 hit), removed with `--delete`. Blob `a6175def87b6` → `cab6af5552aa`.
- Runtime pin: **2 failed / 17 passed**. Both failures name `INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT`: "names a code the vocabulary registers", and the wire code pin's `ApiErrorSchema` parse.
- Restore proven: blob == HEAD.

## Tests (head `5f628a7600`)

**Test suites**
- Full `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime test` (`--project local`): **323 files passed, 4604 passed, 19 skipped**. This run was at `8308116677`. The only later commit, `5f628a7600`, touches two test files, and both were re-run on it.
- Runtime targeted: 6 files, 358 tests.
- Runtime pin file at head: 19/19.
- Client: `automation-resume-refusal-codes.test.ts` 8/8 on rebuilt `dist`, plus `client.test.ts` (216 in the pair before the split).

**Spec**
- `error-code-ledger.test.ts` + `errors.test.ts`: 54.
- Five more ledger-reading tests (`api-error-code-type`, `contract`, `retired-error-codes`, `check-error-code-provenance`, `resume-failure-report.pin`): 100.
- `vitest run --project repo scripts/liveness/evidence.test.ts`: 42.
- No liveness anchor names a touched symbol. The probe `git grep` over `packages/spec/liveness/**` and `*.ledger.*` got 0 hits (exit 1); the control term `errorHandling` hit (exit 0).

**Typecheck and generated artifacts**
- `typecheck` for spec, runtime and client: exit 0. Each package's test layer compiles under its `tsconfig.test.json`; all three runtime test files are in that program, and the debt is unchanged.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated`: all 15 up to date.

**Gates and lint**
- `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:error-status-conformance` and `check:error-code-provenance`: exit 0.
- Full `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`): exit 0 at `5f628a7600`.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `5f628a7600` derived 113 commands, and all 113 ran on that head, all exit 0. The `--ran` reconciliation reads: "113 derived, 113 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN (a DERIVED zero — all 113 recorded an exit code)".
- `check:error-status-conformance` is not in that derivation; it was run separately (exit 0).

## Acceptance notes

- **MCP door's own refusals.** `resume_run`'s own pre-engine refusals still carry status-derived codes: the single not-resumable 404 (unknown, finished or foreign run), the non-screen 409, and the admission 403. That 404 is the door's deliberate non-disclosure answer, and `actions-as-tools.mdx` promises parity only for the engine's answers. So an unknown run answers `RUN_NOT_FOUND` over REST and `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` over MCP. This is an observation, not a contract violation; it is not filed.
- **`PERMISSION_DENIED` row.** Its code equals the 403-derived member, so the code pins cannot distinguish it under ablation. Its registration is still pinned by the vocabulary case.
